evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry identifies 試 as the regular character, records the Shuowen explanation 用也。从言，式聲 and the quotation 明試以功, and gives shì. It lists senses including appoint/use, test, try, and probe, with citations from classical works and later examples. These are dictionary-recorded uses, not a chronology establishing when each sense arose.
evidence.title: [A03817] 試 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, quoting Shuowen and Duan Yucai's commentary
evidence.text: Shuowen analyzes 試 as 从言式聲 and glosses it 用也, citing 明試以功. This is the received historical dictionary's analysis; the inspected entry does not provide earlier inscriptional forms to independently establish the graph's origin.
evidence.title: 說文解字「試」

evidence.field: 試 detailed explanation; historical citations; phonology
evidence.text: The entry presents 試 as a phonosemantic graph 从言，式聲 and gives the base gloss 用／任用. It cites 試，用也 from Shuowen, 明試以功 from the Shangshu tradition, and examples for use, trying, first use, testing, and examination from several classical texts. Its sound section reports Mandarin shì and Middle Chinese category 書母 志韻 去聲, 式吏切; the listed glosses and citations do not by themselves date a semantic transition from use to testing.
evidence.title: 試 shì — 汉典

evidence.field: 式 Shuowen analysis; readings and script forms
evidence.text: The 式 entry gives Shuowen's analysis 从工弋聲 and gloss 法也, reports modern Mandarin shì and Middle Chinese 賞職切, 入聲, and shows later script categories including Chu manuscripts, seal script, Qin slips, and clerical forms. Those data establish a modern reading match with 試 and historical tone/rime information in this dictionary presentation, but not an Old Chinese sound derivation independently checked here.
evidence.title: 式 shì — 汉典

evidence.text: The database identifies the record as 試, U+8A66, gives reading shi4, and lists use, try, first use, examine/test, probe, adverbial ‘try’, a通 form 弒, and surname as dictionary senses. This is lexical metadata and does not demonstrate graphic borrowing or a dated semantic sequence.

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: No inspected primary paleographic source established the earliest graphic form of 試, whether it is attested in oracle-bone or bronze inscriptions, or the proposed alternative depiction; no graphic corruption sequence can be responsibly supplied.

Shuowen reports the early semantic gloss 用 (use/appoint), but the cited 明試以功 is part of a received text whose date and manuscript evidence were not established in this search. A dated earliest attestation remains unresolved.

The dictionary's later senses include try, test and examination, with examples spanning classical and later literature, but the semantic pathways and first attestations for each extension were not established; a gloss list is not chronology.

A sound-component interpretation 言 + 式 is explicitly attributed to Shuowen and repeated in modern dictionaries. The sound match is current Mandarin shì for both, but historical comparison is incomplete: supplied Baxter–Sagart row covers 試 only, and Unihan official pages failed to load.

The suggested Old Chinese derivational account of 試 as a suffixed or exoactive form related to 式 is not independently established here. No separate source-word/depicited-object phonetic-loan claim was supported, so no object-name reconstruction is inferred.

Official Unicode Unihan pages for U+8A66 and U+8BD5 were attempted but unavailable through the web tool; only 試 has a local kMandarin row supplied in the input. The local file is not represented as an external source.

The source inspected for 試 did not explicitly establish that 试 is the standardized simplified counterpart or that 言 → 讠 is the relevant standardization history; the simplified_form relationship needs a directly supporting reference.

No primary paleographic source inspected here establishes the earliest graphic form of 試, whether it occurs in oracle-bone or bronze inscriptions, or a sequence involving graphic corruption. The proposed alternative depiction mentioned in the dossier remains unverified.
The received Shuowen gloss 用也 and citation 明試以功 are not independently dated here to an excavated manuscript. The earliest securely dated attestation of the graph and word-use remains unresolved.

Dictionary examples associate 試 with use/appointment, trying, testing, probing, and examination, but they do not establish first occurrence or a complete semantic pathway among these senses. The received-text citations themselves require textual dating before they can serve as dated attestations.

The phonetic-role claim is the received Shuowen account, with modern Mandarin and supplied Baxter–Sagart row comparison as checks. Unicode pages were inaccessible; the local readings were checked but are not external evidence. The Baxter–Sagart rows do not by themselves prove the proposed derivational morphology.

No exact, inspected Commons file or Xiaoxuetang 試 glyph image with direct URL and verified reuse terms was found. Therefore no historical glyph image is proposed. Search results for unrelated character images were excluded.
The opened CUHK entry records 試 linked to 试 as its simplified counterpart, but no inspected source explicitly documents the standardization relation or the component-level 言 → 讠 change.

limitations.text: No character-specific historical glyph image is shown, so the early written forms of 試 and any graphic change cannot be verified here.
